newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MILAN FALL BACK ON OLD GUARD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MILAN FALL BACK ON OLD GUARD.

text.p: AC Milan might have a new generation of champions waiting in the wings but coach Oscar Washington Tabarez can still turn to the Old Guard in his hour of need.

Just 24 hours after signing Sweden's Jesper Blomqvist from IFK Gothenburg and with the club reportedly chasing Bayern Munich's Christian Ziege, Tabarez is set to recall veterans Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio for Sunday's serie A showdown with Juventus.

The 36-year-old Baresi appears to have finally shrugged off the ankle injury that has limited him to 90 minutes of first division football this season, while Baggio's recent return to form makes it hard for Tabarez to keep him on the bench.
Former Italy international Baresi, who made his debut in April 1978, came through a practice match on Thursday and is ready to extend his record number of appearances for Milan to 507.
Baresi's reassuring presence will restore confidence and cohesion to a side that has lost three league matches in eight outings as well as twice in the Champions' League.
"We have to start playing like a team again," said Baresi, expected to retire at the end of the current season.

Baggio's seven goals in league and cup matches this season, including an inspired effort against Vicenza in the Italian Cup quarter-final on Tuesday, should win him back an automatic first-team place.
According to one report, club president Silvio Berlusconi is personally lobbying for the player's inclusion on Sunday.
The former Juventus player was relegated to the substitute's bench by the prolific partnership between Liberian George Weah and Marco Simone.
"I've refound my goal-scoring form," said Baggio this week, "and I'm really motivated about playing against my old team mates."
Alongside Baggio and Baresi, Dutchman Michael Reiziger, signed from Ajax in the close season, should make his league debut for Milan at right-back in place of the suspended Christian Panucci.
The only negative news came from Marcel Desailly, still recovering from injury in the draw with Vicenza; Stefano Eranio remains on standby to fill-in for the French international.
After a poor start to the defence of their league title, Milan lie fifth in the table, two points behind Juventus and four adrift of leaders Internazionale.
But the aftermath of Juve's shock 3-0 home defeat to Inter in the Italian Cup this week suggests the Italian champions can revive their title ambitions in Turin.
Italian newspapers likened coach Marcello Lippi's reaction to the Inter debacle to "an inquisition".
"He didn't say much in the dressing room after the defeat," one unnamed source told Gazzetta dello Sport, "to speak too much is too dangerous in that kind of tension."
Instead, Lippi saved his wrath for Thursday's training session, repeatedly raising his voice to barrack his players.

Wednesday's setback was especially embarrassing for Lippi because it came after he had conceded a three-day break following a lethargic draw with Napoli and a lacklustre win over third division Nocerina in the Italian Cup.
"To be honest, I planned the break with something else in mind," said Lippi, who has never lost to Milan at the "Delle Alpi" stadium in his two seasons with Juventus.
The coach's worries are heightened by the absence on Sunday of central defenders Paolo Montero and Ciro Ferrara through suspension and left-back Gianluca Pessotto with injury.
The problem has been exacerbated by the lack of specialist defenders in the Juventus squad.

On Sunday, Alessio Tacchinardi, without a full league match all season will anchor the defence while Mark Iuliano, a signing from second division Salernitana, will mark European footballer of the year Weah.

The match with Milan kicks-off a key part of the season for Juventus: in the next week, the European champions face Manchester United at Old Trafford in the Champions' League and the Intercontinental Cup final with Argentine club River Plate in Tokyo.
The "Delle Alpi" stadium should be full to its 71,000 capacity for Sunday's match -- a game that many fans consider has superceded Juventus and Inter as the "Italian Derby".
